claim: A SQLite MCP server exposes list_tables/describe_table tools, a read-only query tool gated to SELECT/PRAGMA/EXPLAIN/WITH, schemas, and canned analysis prompts.
quote: comprehensive SQLite database interaction capabilities ... The query tool is read-only by default, accepting only SELECT, PRAGMA, EXPLAIN, and WITH commands in readonly mode.

claim: Resources are read-only data identified by a unique URI that an MCP server makes available to clients, distinct from tools.
quote: Resources represent any kind of data that an MCP server wants to make available to clients, and each resource is identified by a unique URI and can contain either text or binary data.

claim: MCP sampling flips the flow: the server asks the client's LLM to run a completion, letting a server act like an agent without its own LLM key or inference.
quote: MCP sampling lets servers ask the AI for help ... Rather than clients always initiating requests, servers can ask for AI help when needed.

claim: Several MCP-relevant public APIs need no API key: Open-Meteo weather, Hacker News (firebaseio/Algolia endpoints), Wikipedia, Reddit.
quote: no API keys required, including global news, crypto markets, weather, earthquakes, Reddit, Hacker News, and Wikipedia trends.

claim: The official TypeScript SDK ships server libraries for tools/resources/prompts, stdio and Streamable HTTP transports, and auth helpers.
quote: ships MCP server libraries (tools/resources/prompts, Streamable HTTP, stdio, auth helpers) and MCP client libraries.

claim: The official build-server tutorial builds a weather server exposing get_alerts and get_forecast tools, wired to a client via stdio.
quote: a simple MCP weather server that exposes two tools: get_alerts and get_forecast.

claim: Among the official reference servers, only Everything bundles prompts, resources, and tools together; the rest are specialized (Fetch, Filesystem, Git, Memory, Sequential Thinking, Time).
quote: Everything - Comprehensive test server with prompts, resources, and tools.

claim: The McpServer high-level API exposes registerTool/registerResource/registerPrompt and auto-handles capability negotiation and Zod input validation.
quote: The McpServer provides ergonomic methods like registerTool(), registerResource(), and registerPrompt(). It automatically handles capability negotiation, request routing, and input validation.

claim: MCP provides three first-class context types: Tool (executable action), Resource (read-only data), Prompt (reusable template), each with list and get/call methods.
quote: MCP provides three first-class context types: Tool (executable action), Resource (read-only data), or Prompt (reusable template), each with standardised list and get/call methods.

claim: Open-Meteo is a free, open-source weather API requiring no API keys, suitable for a keyless MCP demo.
quote: Open-Meteo is a free, open-source weather API that doesn't require API keys.

claim: The TypeScript SDK supports sampling, form elicitation, and URL elicitation (for OAuth/API-key/payment flows), with runnable examples in the repo.
quote: URL elicitation allows servers to ask users to complete secure flows in a browser (for example, API key entry, payments, OAuth).

claim: MCP elicitations let a tool pause mid-call to request structured input from the user, enabling multi-turn interactive tools instead of all-upfront parameters.
quote: MCP's elicitations enable your MCP tools to have interactive conversations with users, gathering input dynamically rather than requiring all parameters upfront.

claim: Demo-buildable MCP ideas include a markdown/PDF converter exposing converted files as resources, plus web scrapers and todo-sync servers.
quote: Markdown Converter ... Primitives: Tools (convert file type), Resources (processed files) ... Transform PDFs or videos to markdown.

claim: The official Git reference server provides tools to read, search, and manipulate Git repositories, a model for a repo-insights demo.
quote: Git - Tools to read, search, and manipulate Git repositories.

claim: Microsoft maintains a browser-automation MCP server that navigates pages, clicks, fills forms, screenshots, and runs E2E tests.
quote: A real browser MCP from Microsoft that is actively maintained navigates pages, clicks buttons, fills forms, takes screenshots, and runs end-to-end tests.

claim: Sampling requests are made via createMessage and let servers delegate reasoning to the client LLM; client support is not universal.
quote: MCP sampling allows servers to request LLM completions through the client, enabling sophisticated agentic behaviors while maintaining security and privacy.
